_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 2 Mathematics unit lecture film, Lesson 1 Tens and Ones. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow the lesson opener's three lecture parts (tens and ones; rounding; arrays and sharing), opened out with the lesson page's own numbers: 34 built as 3 tens and 4 ones (step 7, Build it with tens and ones), 34 and 35 rounded on the decade line (step 10), 2 rows of 5 (step 16, Arrays), and 12 sweets shared between 3 friends and grouped into bags of 4 (step 18, Sharing and grouping).
title: Tens and Ones
subtitle: Grade 2 Mathematics
objectives: Understand and explain that the value of each digit in a 2-digit number is determined by its position in that number, recognising zero as a place holder.
Compose, decompose and regroup 2-digit numbers, using tens and ones.
Understand multiplication as: repeated addition an array.
Understand division as: sharing (number of items per group) grouping (number of groups).

beats.say: This is the number 34. It is built from tens and ones.
Every digit has a place. Its place says what it is worth.
Here is 34 in blocks. You can see exactly what it is made of.
Three long rods stand on the left. Each rod is one whole ten.
Count the tens along the row: ten, twenty, thirty.
Beside them sit four small cubes. Each cube is worth just one.
Thirty and four make 34. So 34 is 3 tens and 4 ones.
One rod is worth ten of those cubes. A ten is ten times a one.
Now let us change the blocks. Five rods, and six cubes beside them.
That is 5 tens and 6 ones. The number we built is 56.
The 5 is worth fifty, not five. The 6 is worth only six.
Now take every cube away. Seven rods are left, and no cubes at all.
Seven tens and zero ones is 70. The zero holds the ones place.

at.zero: The zero holds the ones place

beats.say: Rounding means finding the nearest ten. Here is a number line.
Put 34 on it. You can see it sits between 30 and 40.
Count back four steps to reach 30. Count on six steps to reach 40.
Four is fewer than six. So 34 rounds down to 30, not up.
35 sits right in the middle. Five always rounds up, to 40.
An array is rows and columns of things. Every row is the same size.
Here are 2 rows of counters. Each row holds 5 of them.
Five and five make ten. So 2 rows of 5 is 10 counters.
Turn the whole array round. Now it is 5 rows of 2.
That is 5 lots of 2. It is still 10 counters altogether.
Division is sharing out fairly. It is also making equal groups.
Share 12 sweets between 3 friends. One each, round and round.
Everybody ends up with 4 sweets. So 12 shared by 3 is 4.
Now take the same 12 sweets. Group them into bags of 4.
One bag, two bags, three bags. Nothing is left over.
So 12 in groups of 4 makes 3 bags, with none left.
A 2-digit number is tens and ones. 34 is 3 tens and 4 ones.
Rounding finds the nearest ten. So 34 rounds down to 30.
An array shows times. Look: 2 rows of 5 is 10 counters.
Sharing and grouping are both division. Now go and build some numbers.
